I will keep it simple and steady this year. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will follow the pattern I trust most: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. At my age, I do not want to spread myself across many crops or take market risk on something unfamiliar. Wheat and maize fit my land, my experience, and our local water and weather conditions. I will use better seed, not old farm-saved seed, because I want stable emergence and yield. I will fertilize enough to keep yields reliable but not push too hard, because fertilizer is expensive and too much can waste money. I will irrigate wheat more carefully because it needs water at key stages, and I will keep maize management simpler and faster after wheat harvest. I will use rotary tillage for wheat land preparation, then no-tillage for maize after wheat so I can save labor and catch the sowing window. I will spray only as needed, mainly for common disease and insect pressure, because I want to protect yield without adding unnecessary cost.
